newsitem.title: CHINA: New harbour opens northwest of Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: New harbour opens northwest of Shanghai.

text.p: A new harbour in Changshou, a satellite city northwest of Shanghai, has opened and would mainly serve a Singapore-invested industrial park in Suzhou, the Wen Hui Bao newspaper said on Sunday.

Changshou harbour, which opened on Saturday, occupies six square kilometres and includes three 3,500-tonne piers for coal and other commodities, three 5,000-tonne piers for petrochemicals and other oil products as well as warehouses, it said.
Three of the piers are joint ventures between the local port authority and Hong Kong and Singapore companies, it said but did not name the companies.
Earlier this year the Chinese and Singapore governments jointly nominated Changshou port as an important import and export channel for the Singapore industrial park in Suzhou, Wen Hui Bao said.
Suzhou, about 100 km west of Shanghai, had attracted a large number of Singapore and other foreign investors.
Construction of the port began in 1992, it said but gave no more details.
